comparison: Both address phylogenetic claims (C2-C6) about human-specific F60 residue. OpenEval finds evidence well-supported by phylogenetic alignment and citations. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, requesting 'more full phylogenetic analysis' and asking conclusions be 'cautioned or strengthened by further evidence.'

Both evaluate CARD8 cleavage data (C7, C9-C13). OpenEval finds claims strongly SUPPORTED by immunoblot data in Figures 1B-D. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, questioning validation of the ~45 kDa band, noting 'clear evidence of cleavage in the F60L mutant,' and stating cleavage is 'inefficient.'

Both address species-specific cleavage patterns (C15-C18, C21, C65-C66). OpenEval finds claims well-SUPPORTED by immunoblot data. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, noting additional bands, faint cleavage signals, requesting repeated experiments or in vitro biochemical assays, and reiterating that cleavage is 'inefficient.'

Both address SIVmac239PR substrate specificity (C19, C20, C92). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED despite noting incomplete specificity. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED without specific critique of the supplementary data.

Both evaluate cell death and cytokine data (C23, C24, C26, C27, C29). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by PI uptake and IL-1β assays. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, noting PI staining is 'generic,' effects are 'modest,' and that HIV has pathological impacts independent of PR activity that are difficult to distinguish.

Both address TLR priming requirement for IL-1β secretion (C25, C28, C30). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED, accepting the strict TLR-dependence for IL-1β secretion, though requesting extension to primary macrophages.

Both evaluate CARD8 and CASP1 dependence (C31-C34). OpenEval finds claims well-SUPPORTED by knockout experiments with multiple virus strains. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, stating effects are 'modest,' requesting experiments in primary CD4 T cells, and noting lack of evidence in 'primary viral target cells.'

Both address early response timing (C35-C38) and mechanism (C52-C54 in OpenEval R9). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by time-course and inhibitor data. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, requesting earlier time points (<12hrs) or RT/integration blocks to distinguish incoming virion protease from de novo viral protein synthesis.

Both address lopinavir inhibition and ΔVpr data (C39-C42). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED without challenging the lopinavir or ΔVpr findings.

Both evaluate complementation experiments (C43-C50). OpenEval finds claims strongly SUPPORTED by doxycycline-inducible system and species-swap experiments. Peer reviewers find evidence UNCERTAIN, requesting verification with wild-type HIV-1 instead of only VSV-G, testing SIVcpz with chimpanzee CARD8, and creating other non-human primate CARD8 proteins.

OpenEval R9 addresses mechanistic model (C51-C57) finding claims SUPPORTED though detection of packaged protease is 'inferential.' Peer R7 addresses timing claims (C35-C38, C52-C54) finding evidence UNCERTAIN due to inability to distinguish incoming from newly synthesized protease. Partial overlap on mechanism.

OpenEval R10 addresses TLR priming effects (C58-C63) finding claims SUPPORTED. Peer R5 addresses overlapping TLR claims (C25, C28, C30, C60) also finding them SUPPORTED. Both agree on TLR-dependence for IL-1β secretion.

Both address TLR priming (C58, C59, C62). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with reasonable speculation about in vivo priming. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED without challenging the TLR data or discussion of priming sources.

OpenEval R11 addresses evolutionary timeline and genetic sweep (C64-C70) finding claims SUPPORTED. Peer R3 addresses species-specific cleavage (C15-C18, C21, C65-C66) finding evidence UNCERTAIN. Overlap on C65-C66 regarding evolutionary claims, with peer reviewers requesting conclusions be 'cautioned or strengthened.'

OpenEval addresses CARD8 polymorphism and positive selection (C71-C76), finding C71-C74 SUPPORTED but C75-C76 explicitly speculative and UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific evolutionary speculation claims.

Both address pathogenesis relevance. OpenEval R13 addresses HIV pathogenesis (C77-C86) finding claims SUPPORTED by citations and recent independent work. Peer R9 addresses pathogenesis claims (C82, C90) finding them UNSUPPORTED/speculative, stating effects are 'modest' and conclusions should be 'cautioned or substantiated.'

OpenEval R14 addresses SIV pathogenesis speculation (C87-C91) finding C87-C89 SUPPORTED but C90-C91 explicitly UNCERTAIN/speculative. Peer R9 overlaps on C90, finding pathogenesis conclusions UNSUPPORTED and requiring caution or further experimental data.

Both address SIVcpz pathogenesis in chimpanzees (C87-C88). OpenEval finds C87-C89 SUPPORTED by citations but C90-C91 speculative. Peer reviewers find C87-C88 UNSUPPORTED, stating 'this seems like an overstatement' and noting SIVcpz causes disease in wild chimpanzees (Keele et al., 2009).

OpenEval addresses summary claims (C93-C100) finding them well-SUPPORTED by experimental data throughout manuscript. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these summary claims.

OpenEval addresses background/context claims (C101-C117) finding them SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to established prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
